title: Preventing Strategic Behaviors in Collaborative Inference for Vertical Federated Learning

problem.claim: During collaborative inference in vertical federated learning, parties can strategically alter uploaded local embeddings to influence final predictions.

gap.claim: Current VFL inference systems are vulnerable to strategic behavior, including disruptions to display-opportunity allocation caused by parties' content preferences.

contributions.claim: A distribution-based penalty mechanism is proposed to detect and penalize strategic behavior in collaborative inference by eliciting truthful local embeddings.
The authors theoretically prove that constraining the distribution of uploaded embeddings can prevent dishonest parties from achieving higher utility.
Under mild conditions, the mechanism is shown to admit truth-telling as an asymptotic Bayesian Nash equilibrium.

author_reported_evidence.claim: In a representative federated-recommendation case study, allocation of display opportunities was severely disrupted by parties' preferences in display content.
Experimental results demonstrate reduced dishonest utility increases from strategic behavior and more truthful uploading of local embeddings.

narrative_sequence.summary: VFL enables collaborative use of private features distributed across multiple parties.
Inference requires parties to upload local embeddings, which can be strategically altered to influence predictions.
A federated-recommendation case study shows severe disruption of display-opportunity allocation under strategic preferences.
The proposed mechanism uses distribution-based penalties and statistical two-sample tests, deactivating dishonest uploads.
The authors report theoretical equilibrium behavior and experiments indicating reduced dishonest utility gains and more truthful uploads.

source_observation.claim: Constraining the distribution of uploaded embeddings is presented as a way to limit dishonest parties' utility gains.

interpretation.claim: Monitoring distributional consistency can align submitted intermediate representations with truthful participation.

application.claim: Collaborative inference systems could use statistical two-sample tests as a behavioral-monitoring signal and disable suspicious submissions.

exception.claim: The reported equilibrium guarantee holds only asymptotically and under mild conditions.

unknowns: The specific mild conditions required for the equilibrium result are not stated.
The abstract does not provide datasets, baselines, quantitative results, or experimental settings.
The abstract does not specify the exact distributional tests, penalty form, or deactivation policy.
